paragraphs: Pace Scheduler sells a cloud-based scheduling system built for organizations that keep 24/7 schedules. Its clients include police departments, sheriff's offices, campus security, fire departments and public transportation agencies. Because that client base varies, the system is modular, so a department's site can be built with only the parts it wants.

The company says it designed the software to be easy to use without dropping the advanced features needed to maintain round-the-clock schedules. A mobile app is included, so staff can view schedules and submit or handle requests from an iOS or Android device as well as from a PC or tablet. In testimonials on the site, departments describe using it to fill shifts, request time off and balance leave banks. One says the shift bidding feature cut a process that used to take a month and a half down to four days.

Those testimonials come from agencies such as Tipp City PD in Ohio, Hudson PD in Colorado, Santa Paula PD in California and the Monroe County Sheriff's Office in Michigan, which says deputies, corrections officers and support staff all use it. Several describe replacing paper or Excel spreadsheets, and one lieutenant says the program replaced over a dozen spreadsheets. The company offers a free online demo to organizations that ask.
